thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (streaming). p95=420ms -> 1.6s, p99=1.1s -> 5.8s. SLO breach threshold crossed. Auto-page: @emma (oncall)

emma (oncall): taking it. seeing a few customer errors reported, tagging here.

sanjay: on the metrics dashboard now — tail latency climbs at 12:03 UTC, sustained for ~6m. Throughput steady. No config deploys in that window (checked deploy-bot).

lee: logs show a rash of streaming stalls: clients time out while waiting for tokens. I can reproduce locally by hitting the streaming endpoint -> chunk delays of 3-6s.

maria: any node-level alerts? I see Node GPU temperature warnings in infra-alerts channel earlier.

ops-bot: node-gpu-telemetry-prod-17 reported: ECC_ERRORS incremented, NVML warnings, GPU clock throttled to 300MHz due to thermal constraint.

emma (oncall): ok, SSHing to node-gpu-telemetry-prod-17 now. grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi.

lee: quick customer impact check: about 2.3% of requests in last 10m had streaming stalls >2s. High-traffic routes for small-token chat affected more.

sanjay: paste of nvidia-smi -q excerpt: ```
=============== NVSMI LOG ===============
GPU 0:
  Temperature
    GPU Current Temp                     : 95 C
  Xid Errors
    Gpu Access Error (Xid 81)            : 12
  Perf State                            : P0
  Clocks Throttle Reasons               : HW Slowdown
  Applications Clocks                   : 300 MHz
```

maria: kernel logs showing repeated NVRM Xid 13 and Xid 81 messages: ```
[ 12:03:45.123 ] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:af:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12:03:45.128 ] NVRM: Xid (PCI:af:00): 31, 0000(0x0000001f)
[ 12:04:01.901 ] NVRM: Xid (PCI:af:00): 81, 0000(0x00000051)
```

emma (oncall): so hardware errors + thermal. Could be flaky GPU or cooling failure. Priority: mitigate customer latency first, then remediate node.

lee: mitigation plan — migrate active model shards off node-gpu-telemetry-prod-17, cordon & drain, scale up spare pool to keep throughput. If drain stalls due to stuck lipid (kv cache?) use force-restart on serving process.

emma (oncall): running kubectl: ```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-telemetry-prod-17
kubectl drain node-gpu-telemetry-prod-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

ops-bot: cordon successful. Drain in progress; several pods stuck in Terminating due to open streaming connections.

sanjay: while drain is happening, enabling overflow routing to fallback model variant in eu-west to relieve pressure: updating smart-router policy.

maria: policy change applied. Traffic diverted 25% -> fallback (lower memory) model, and 10% traffic to dedicated backup region. Should reduce tail load.

emma (oncall): I'm seeing p99 drop from 5.8s -> 2.1s after routing shift. p95 back to ~480ms. Still SLO breach for p99 but improving.

lee: pods stuck because of streaming connections — using graceful shutdown didn't close client streams. Will kill process with SIGKILL on node to free sessions and let k8s reschedule.

emma (oncall): executing remote: ```
sudo pkill -9 -f "redwood-serving" || true
# follow up: restart node exporter and nv-hostengine after reboot
```

ops-bot: process kill freed the pods, drain completed. Node marked unschedulable.

sanjay: telemetry shows GPU ECC errors stop being reported after processes killed. But temp remains high, fan speed low response. Likely a failing fan or thermal sensor.

maria: PV customers: flagged high-impact customers in status page draft. Need short note: degraded performance for streaming endpoints, mitigation in progress, some requests delayed.

emma (oncall): writing status update now. Draft: "Investigating increased latency affecting streaming responses due to GPU degradation on a host. We have diverted traffic and removed the host from serving. Some customers may have experienced slow responses during the incident window. We will provide follow-up after hardware investigation." Approve?

lee: approve. Add ETA for next update in 60m.

emma (oncall): raising a hardware ticket with infra: node-gpu-telemetry-prod-17 — request RMA if fan/board failing. Attaching logs and nvml dumps.

ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-1937. Suggested immediate hardware action: RMA or move node to maintenance for diagnostics.

sanjay: post-mitigation metrics: p99 reduced to 850ms and holding; p95 380ms. Error rate normalized.

maria: customer impact summary for postmortem: window 12:03–12:12 UTC, approx 2.3% of requests affected, peak p99 5.8s, cause: GPU thermal throttling + ECC errors leading to hardware-level performance degradation. Mitigation: traffic diversion, cordon & drain, process restart, node OOS for hardware triage. Next: RMA and hardware test farm run.

emma (oncall): leaving oncall handoff note — I'll keep monitoring for 30m, then hand to next oncall @lee at 12:50 UTC if stable. If p99 creeps above 1.5s re-alert.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident state -> mitigated (ongoing hardware maintenance).

sanjay: will add kernel/NV driver versions and full nvml dumps to the postmortem. Also suggest adding automations: detect ECC error rate thresholds to preemptively move workloads.

lee: thanks team. Follow-up items: postmortem writeup, infra RMA, automation ticket for ECC preemption.

emma (oncall): thanks all — updating incident channel and status page.
